<h1>Every step on the board, until it clicks.</h1>
<p class="lede">I have taught calculus, differential equations, precalculus, algebra, trigonometry, and actuarial mathematics as an instructor of record, recitation leader, lab assistant, and grader. In every role I aim for clear reasoning, plenty of worked examples, and a room where students are comfortable asking the next question.</p>
<p style="color:var(--muted)">This fall I lead <strong>Calculus III</strong> recitations at Iowa State University. We work through vectors, partial derivatives, multiple integrals, and vector calculus by solving problems together.</p>

<div class="stat-row"><div><b>8</b><span>courses taught</span></div><div><b>3</b><span>universities</span></div><div><b>2018</b><span>first classroom</span></div></div>

<div class="award"><i class="bi bi-award"></i><span><strong>Distinguished Teaching Assistant Award</strong>, Florida State University, April 2026</span></div>

<article class="course now">
<div class="code">Calculus III<span class="inst">Iowa State University</span></div>
<div>
<h3>Calculus III</h3>
<p>Vectors, vector-valued functions, functions of several variables, partial derivatives, multiple integrals, and vector calculus. In recitation I reinforce lecture material through guided examples and collaborative problem solving, helping students turn geometric intuition into precise analytical technique.</p>
<div class="terms"><a href="teaching/fall26.html"><b>Fall 2026</b> · Recitation Instructor</a></div>
</div>
</article>

<article class="course">
<div class="code">MAP 2302<span class="inst">Florida State University</span></div>
<div>
<h3>Ordinary Differential Equations</h3>
<p>Differential equations as models of evolving systems: direction fields, first-order methods, second-order linear equations, systems, Laplace transforms, power-series solutions, and introductory numerical methods. Students learn to read an equation's structure, choose a method, verify solutions, and interpret qualitative behavior.</p>
<div class="terms"><a href="teaching/summer26-map2302.html"><b>Summer 2026</b> · Instructor of Record</a></div>
</div>
</article>

<article class="course">
<div class="code">MAC 2312<span class="inst">Florida State University</span></div>
<div>
<h3>Calculus with Analytic Geometry II</h3>
<p>Techniques and applications of integration, differential equations, sequences, infinite series, power series, and Taylor series. The course runs on structured notes, worked examples, and practice tests, with step-by-step discussion of each one.</p>
<div class="terms"><a href="teaching/fall25.html"><b>Fall 2025</b> · Instructor of Record</a><a href="teaching/sp26.html"><b>Spring 2026</b> · Instructor of Record</a></div>
</div>
</article>

<article class="course">
<div class="code">MAC 2311<span class="inst">Florida State University</span></div>
<div>
<h3>Calculus with Analytic Geometry I</h3>
<p>Limits and continuity, derivatives and rates of change, optimization, curve sketching, integrals, and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. I taught through guided examples, active-learning problems, poster presentations, and targeted feedback.</p>
<div class="terms"><a href="teaching/fall22.html"><b>Fall 2022</b> · Recitation Instructor</a><a href="teaching/sp25.html"><b>Spring 2025</b> · Instructor of Record</a><a href="teaching/summer25.html"><b>Summer 2025</b> · Instructor of Record</a></div>
</div>
</article>

<article class="course">
<div class="code">MAP 4170<span class="inst">Florida State University</span></div>
<div>
<h3>Introduction to Actuarial Mathematics</h3>
<p>The financial mathematics behind actuarial practice and professional exams: accumulation and discount functions, nominal and effective rates, equations of value, annuities, loans, and bonds. It draws on my own background in actuarial exams and the life-insurance industry.</p>
<div class="terms"><a href="teaching/fall23.html"><b>Fall 2023</b> · Grader</a><a href="teaching/sp24.html"><b>Spring 2024</b> · Instructor of Record</a></div>
</div>
</article>

<article class="course">
<div class="code">MAC 1140<span class="inst">Florida State University</span></div>
<div>
<h3>Precalculus Algebra</h3>
<p>Function-based reasoning for calculus: complex numbers; polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions; inequalities; and inverse functions. The course stresses multiple representations and careful algebra over memorized procedures.</p>
<div class="terms"><a href="teaching/fall21.html"><b>Fall 2021 – Spring 2022</b> · Lecture &amp; Lab TA</a><a href="teaching/sp23.html"><b>Spring 2023</b> · Instructor of Record</a></div>
</div>
</article>

<article class="course">
<div class="code">MATH 1510 · 1511<span class="inst">Youngstown State University</span></div>
<div>
<h3>College Algebra and Trigonometry</h3>
<p>Equations, functions, and algebraic modeling, then angles, the unit circle, identities, inverse functions, and periodic behavior. Both courses connect symbolic, graphical, and numerical representations and build students' independence through structured practice.</p>
<div class="terms"><a href="teaching/f18-f21.html"><b>Fall 2018 – Spring 2020</b> · Instructor of Record</a></div>
</div>
</article>
